video_title: FRANCES TIAFOE, MPJ, AND TRAE YOUNG: FROM THE POINT WEEKEND LIVE PODCAST

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his motivation to return to playing
quotes.excerpt: I just want to get back to playing. People have a certain perception of me.
quotes.quote: I just want to get back to playing. For me, I think people have a certain perception of me and may not think I'm what I used to be because I haven't played in a year, just from being injured and then obviously being traded here. I don't think people have been able to see me play. And for me, I've just been training like I'm back in high school again, getting up at 6:00 a.m., getting back on the track, and doing things that I know I used to do and what got me here. I'm super excited. This is a great place to start a new chapter in, and I don't want to let this opportunity go to waste.

quotes.speaker: Trae Young
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young on his leadership role as a veteran
quotes.excerpt: They look at me like somebody who's played in the NBA, who's an All-Star.
quotes.quote: Your first opportunity as a rookie, being 19, you don't have the experience when you come in to have the voice to say certain things and to speak your mind on certain things. But now, going into year nine, I've experienced so many different things that I just know what to do and what not to do. I'm able to give these guys advice, but they also look at me differently. They look at me like somebody who's played in the NBA, who's an All-Star, who's been All-NBA. They look at me like a veteran. It's easy to be a leader on a team like that, and that's what's so exciting about this chapter and this team. It's not just going to be me that leads us to win; it's a collective.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his humble beginnings and underdog mentality
quotes.excerpt: It's never about where you start, it's about where you're going.
quotes.quote: It's super humbling, and obviously, coming from this area, we definitely have that underdog mentality. It's never about where you start, it's about where you're going. And obviously, I feel like I'm a huge product of that. But to be able to see them enjoy all the great success and matches and the arenas is what it means. To have little kids like y'all want to inspire to do something special because of people like myself and Trae, so that's what it's ultimately about.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his early realization of becoming a pro
quotes.excerpt: I was like, 'Yeah, I think I'm going to do the thing.'
quotes.quote: There's a time where everybody is wishful, like, 'Oh yeah, you're young, you want to go to the NBA.' For me, I was like, 'Yeah, I want to be a pro.' But you get that time where the homies start saying you're nice, and then you start proving it up. And then I was like, 'Yeah, I think I'm going to do the thing.' When I was 11, 12, parents think you're talking crazy, and then a few years later, you get a little growth spurt, and then here I am.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on the prestige of Wimbledon
quotes.excerpt: To me, the best event still in the world is Wimbledon.
quotes.quote: To me, the best event still in the world is Wimbledon. If you guys have never been there, that's an amazing tournament here in the area. But like, there's nothing, honestly, to me, the best event still in the world is Wimbledon. If you guys never get there in the summertime, like, it's, I mean, the Augusta of tennis. Everything is super pristine, wearing all white, and I'm not even like the biggest traditional guy with that, but I'm like, you can feel the history and stuff, and that would be something really cool to win.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on the physical demands of tennis
quotes.excerpt: There's no clock, so you don't know how long the match is going to be.
quotes.quote: Receiving the serve is crazy. I mean, obviously, you guys know me playing badminton, serving at 158 miles an hour, it's pretty, it's pretty tough to do. But I think just the biggest thing is that there's no clock, so you don't know how long the match is going to be. So prepping is like, you know, we can play for four hours, five hours, and then kind of have to come back and do it in a couple days' time. So I think that's the biggest toughest thing to prepare for, but I think the actual play is definitely returning serve.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on maintaining a flow state during matches
quotes.excerpt: I try to always be in flow state and kind of just treat it like another moment.
quotes.quote: Hopefully in that moment it's nothing, because the more you're thinking, the worse the worse it happens. I try to always be in flow state and kind of just treat it like another moment, like, and trust the work that you've done and just try to do it one more time. But yeah, of course, when you get in those moments you haven't been before, you're super excited and you're like, 'Man, I'm about to be my idol, like Nadal, I have this guy on my poster, like, I'm about to send him home,' like that's fire. But I try to just be in the moment and not make it as big as it seems because, you know, tennis, you can win a big big match, but you got to still prove it up the next round.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his long-term impact on tennis
quotes.excerpt: When I'm done, I want to leave impact that there's a lot more people like me playing tennis.
quotes.quote: It's definitely a lot of weight, you know. You want to keep, you know, inspiring because, you know, when I'm done, I want to leave impact that there's a lot more people like me playing tennis. And obviously, it is a deeper conversation that we're making more accessible and what have you, but that's, that's kind of the goal. So when I walk out there, I want to make it cool, I want to like even have swag and, you know, show your personality and get pumped up and, you know, have different inspiration from other sports.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his goal to win a major
quotes.excerpt: I want to win, you know, a major.
quotes.quote: I want to win, you know, a major. I want to bring one to this area, you know, a US Open, Wimbledon, I'm not picky, whatever case may be, French Open. Want to be number one in the world. I think those two things are really realistic. I guess crack back in the top 10, being number eight, so I think, let's just not be comfortable and try to and try to chase those things. But yeah, I mean, I'm just trying to do what Trae is trying to do here, bringing it back to the city. I think there's no secret to that.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his early chemistry with Trae Young
quotes.excerpt: It doesn't feel like it was 10, 11 years ago that we were doing that.
quotes.quote: It was an unforgettable time. I mean, it doesn't feel like it was 10, 11 years ago that we were doing that, you know? It feels like the other day that we met and we kind of developed that bond and developed that chemistry on the court. And I mean, yeah, it's undeniable that we're one of the best AAU teams. I don't think there's been a team that's gone to Peach Jam and had that margin of victory. I mean, we were beating every team by 30 on our way to a Peach Jam championship. So I think it's merited, and you know, he's the best point guard I've I've played with.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on the competitiveness of the modern NBA
quotes.excerpt: The NBA just keeps getting better and better and better.
quotes.quote: The NBA just keeps getting better and better and better, you know? Even going into this year, I think there's probably 10 teams that can win a championship, you know what I mean? So I'm on a team now where we're trying to build. We got a lot of young a lot of young players that are are getting better, and you know, we got Julius and me over here is kind of the veteran guys, Terrence, man, that are leading the charge. But right now, it's a completely different role as it was in Denver, and we're just trying to build and and do it the right way, you know? Washington was in a similar place for the last few years, last several years, and now they finally got a team that they feel like can go for it, and kind of that's what we're trying to build over there in Brooklyn as well.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his championship run with the Nuggets
quotes.excerpt: That finals run with the Nuggets actually reminds me of our Peach Jam run.
quotes.quote: That finals run with the Nuggets actually reminds me of our Peach Jam run, just the fact that we were smacking everybody. Like, that run with Denver, we we went on a I think we lost three games that playoffs, three, four games, you know, swept the Lakers, and we won the finals in five games. It was a it was an amazing run with an amazing team, but the NBA just keeps getting better and better and better.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on the youth movement in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: The league is getting younger, you know what I mean?
quotes.quote: The league is getting younger, you know what I mean? The Spurs are such a young team and they were just in the finals. Oklahoma City was a very young team, and so it just kind of shows that, you know, you can turn things around quick, and the playstyle's up and down, you know? It's less half-court, it's more up and down, so having those young young guys that that want to do that is huge, especially, you know, for for me and the way I like to play and shoot threes and transition threes, things like that.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on the impact of NIL on college basketball
quotes.excerpt: If I was getting paid millions of dollars, yeah, I would have stayed in college.
quotes.quote: If I was getting paid millions of dollars, yeah, I would have stayed in college for sure. I would have kicked it with the fam and took my time, definitely. I don't need to have $10 million in college, though, honestly. I didn't I didn't need that. I don't know what I would have done with with millions of dollars in college. It was a blessing in disguise. We didn't have I don't know, I mean, I I don't I don't think we were the people to have have that money in college and be locked in, so I think also, too, you know, you're seeing guys stay a little bit longer in college because maybe they're not lottery in in you all situations or on the cusp of lottery, but, you know, who fall into that maybe that 20 to 40 range, go back to school.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on his back injury and faith
quotes.excerpt: I went through so much crazy stuff that like I had to rely on my faith.
quotes.quote: I went through so much crazy stuff that like I had to rely on my faith. Like, I think that before I got injured, I thought everything was in my hands, you know? I'm the number one player, I'm supposed to be projected the top one or two draft pick and I'm everything was easy for me my whole life. Then I hit that adversity and I was told by so many different doctors and people that I I might not ever play again, you know? And I'm like, basketball was my only option, my only plan and I was told I was never going to play again, so I kind of had to like rely on God, like, 'Yo, this is out of my hands, if if you want me to play then give me the strength to continue to play, but if not, show me another route to go.'

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Sr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Sr. on the meaning of being different
quotes.excerpt: Can you explain to the kids what it means to not be a follower and to be different?
quotes.quote: I noticed you like to use the phrase 'be different.' Can you explain to the kids what it means to not be a follower and to be different?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Sr.
text_blocks.text: I noticed you like to use the phrase 'be different.' Can you explain to the kids what it means to not be a follower and to be different?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: Yeah, definitely a phrase of mine that I I like to use. I like to be different. I've always liked to be different. It's just a phrase more just so like, if somebody's it more stood out to me on like the fact of like, if somebody's doing something bad, like I I don't want to necessarily follow that. Like, it's okay to be different. Usually the the most crowded rooms are the the rooms you don't want to be in, and for me, like that's what it it is for me is just being different and standing out, and it's okay to be different.
